acceptanceCriteria: Decide and record (spec amendment or build-log decision) whether nested member order is normative; if it is, CEM-V1-109 is amended to state it.
If normative: one consumer is aligned, and a sealed vector compares the full rendered result bytes from both consumers, including nested drift, hunks and references.
If not normative: the packet text states that consumers must not depend on nested order, and a test shows the digest is independent of it.
Focused tests in internal/cem and interop/cem01-go, with sealed change evidence.
body: Found by the V1-1333 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#879, seal 9eb1815c0) on 2026-10-14 while sealing protocol/cem-1.0/stable/citation-vectors. The native verifier (internal/cem) and the portable consumer (interop/cem01-go) agree on top-level result member order, on citation block bytes and on verdictSha256. They emit the nested members of drift, hunks and references in different orders. CEM-V1-109 (proposed in #879) states that nested order is not fixed, so the vectors compare only the digest and citation bytes. Two independent consumers whose rendered output differs byte-for-byte below the top level weaken the packet's 'reproduce byte for byte' claim and invite consumer-specific parsers. Related but distinct: V1-1289 (refusal-code divergence).
title: cem/1.0 consumers emit nested drift, hunks and references members in different orders
